descriptionChirho: An adjective describing a person or thing as lacking righteousness, acting unjustly, or being morally wicked; used substantivally for 'the unrighteous' who will not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:1, 6:9) and predicatively of God ('Is God unjust?' Romans 3:5) or of unjust stewards (Luke 16:10-11) and unrighteous mammon (Luke 16:11). Spanish injusto/injustos, Arabic ظَالِمٌ/الظّالِمينَ (zalim/az-zalimin), Korean 불의한 (bul-uihan), Hindi अन्यायी/अधर्मी (anyayi/adharmi), Swahili dhalimu/wasio-haki. The two clusters differ only in number: plural substantival forms (S61342, 7x) versus singular forms (S61341, 5x), with no real semantic difference.
